title: Before Belfast, There Is Dambulla. India's Next Generation Starts Tomorrow.
excerpt: Sooryavanshi, Tilak Varma and 13 others open India A's tri-series in Sri Lanka on Monday. For some, it's the last audition before the senior tour.
body:
India's next generation of cricketers has landed in Dambulla, and the stakes are higher than any A-team tour in recent memory.

The India A squad, captained by Tilak Varma with Ruturaj Gaikwad as vice-captain, will open its campaign against Sri Lanka A on Monday at the Rangiri Dambulla International Cricket Stadium. Afghanistan A completes the three-team field in a double round-robin that runs through June 21, with the top two sides meeting in the final.

## The Sooryavanshi Factor

Every eye will be on Vaibhav Sooryavanshi. The 15-year-old broke Chris Gayle's record for most sixes in an IPL season, hammered 776 runs at a strike rate of 237.30 for Rajasthan Royals, and became the first player in IPL history to win both MVP and Best Emerging Player in the same campaign. The BCCI rewarded him with a maiden senior T20I call-up for the Ireland and England tours later this month.

But before Belfast and Birmingham, there is Dambulla. This tri-series is Sooryavanshi's first taste of one-day international cricket at any level, a format that demands patience alongside power. The selectors, and the millions of NRI cricket fans who watched his IPL fireworks on late-night streams, will want to see how the teenager adapts.

"One of the biggest draws for viewers will be to watch the biggest sensation in Indian cricket, teenage prodigy Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, whose explosive talent is making him one of the most talked-about players today," said Rajesh Kaul of Sony Pictures Networks India, which has acquired broadcast rights for the tournament.

## Squad Reshuffle After Parag Injury

The India A squad underwent two late changes before departing. Harsh Dubey was pulled out after earning a call-up to the senior Test and ODI squads for the Afghanistan series. More significantly, vice-captain Riyan Parag was ruled out with a hamstring injury sustained during the latter stages of IPL 2026 while captaining Rajasthan Royals. He will undergo rehabilitation at the BCCI Centre of Excellence in Bengaluru.

Gaikwad, who led India to gold at the 2023 Asian Games and was recently drafted into the India A side, stepped in as vice-captain. His experience in subcontinental conditions will be valuable in Dambulla's spin-friendly environment.

The full squad reads: Tilak Varma (C), Ruturaj Gaikwad (VC), Priyansh Arya, Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, Ayush Badoni, Nishant Sindhu, Suryansh Shedge, Prabhsimran Singh (WK), Kumar Kushagra (WK), Vipraj Nigam, Yash Thakur, Yudhvir Singh, Anshul Kamboj, Arshad Khan, and Anukul Roy.

## The Coaching Setup

Hrishikesh Kanitkar, Sunil Joshi, Lakshmipathy Balaji, and Shubhadeep Ghosh will coach the side — a blend of former international cricketers and domestic development experts. Their brief is clear: prepare these players for the senior setup.

## What NRIs Should Know

For Indian diaspora viewers who tracked every Sooryavanshi six this IPL season, the tri-series airs live on Sony LIV starting at 10:00 AM IST (12:30 AM EDT, 9:30 PM PDT the night before) across five languages: English, Hindi, Tamil, Telugu, and Kannada.

The schedule unfolds briskly. India A faces Sri Lanka A on June 9, Afghanistan A on June 11, then repeats the cycle before the final on June 21. Seven matches in 13 days, all at the same venue. No excuses for missing form, and no hiding from conditions.

## The Bigger Picture

This is not just about developing young talent. It is about identifying who can handle pressure before the Ireland T20Is on June 26 and the England series starting July 1. For Sooryavanshi, a strong showing could fast-track his debut under Shreyas Iyer's captaincy. For Varma and Gaikwad, it is a chance to demonstrate leadership credentials that the selectors are actively evaluating.

The last time India A toured Sri Lanka for a multi-format series, the graduates included Shubman Gill and Washington Sundar. Both are now Test regulars. The conveyor belt turns again in Dambulla.
